title: How Websites Remember You: Cookies & Login in 60 Seconds 🍪 #shorts
description:
You log in once and a website remembers you for weeks. HTTP forgets you after every request, so when you log in the server checks your password against a stored hash, creates a session, and sends your browser a cookie with a random session ID. Your browser attaches it to every request, so the server knows it's you. Plus HttpOnly and Secure flags, and why cookie banners exist.

lines: You log in once, and the website remembers you for weeks. How?
The web has no memory. To the server, every request is a stranger.
So when you log in, the server checks your password against a stored hash: a scrambled version, never the real thing.
If it matches, it starts a session, and sends your browser a cookie with a random session ID.
Your browser attaches that cookie to every request after that. The server sees the ID, and knows it's you.
That's why login cookies are protected: HttpOnly, so scripts can't steal them, and Secure, so they only travel over HTTPS.
Cookies also remember your cart and language, and can track you across sites. That's why you see cookie banners.
